tasks.title: Security: re-apply the lock, encryption and dark mode on current main
tasks.prompt:
The Tijori React Native app already has a completed security change set on the branch 'jules-6136906809176550882-a55b9ffa' (app lock with passcode + biometric, encryption at rest, real Settings, and a dark/light theme). That branch now CONFLICTS with main, so it cannot be merged.

Task: re-apply that same work cleanly on top of the CURRENT main, and open a fresh pull request.

How: read the files on branch 'jules-6136906809176550882-a55b9ffa' (src/ThemeContext.tsx, src/PasscodeSetupScreen.tsx, src/storage/, src/screens.tsx, src/components.tsx, App.tsx, package.json) to see what was intended. Then integrate those changes with the current main - main already includes Documents, the password generator/vault health, and polish work, so do NOT overwrite those; combine them.

Keep the existing visual language. Make sure the lock really gates the app, data is encrypted at rest, Settings actually works (biometric toggle, change passcode, auto-lock timing defaulting to 1 minute, and a light/dark switch), and the theme context is used across the screens.

Housekeeping: no temporary or patch files (.diff, .patch, .orig, .rej, .bak or editor backups), and no reasoning or thinking-out-loud comments in the code.

Constraints: TypeScript; npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test must pass. react-native-keychain and crypto-js are already allowed.

tasks.title: Data integrity and secure randomness fixes
tasks.prompt:
Fix data-integrity and security-hardening issues in the Tijori React Native app (React Native 0.81.5, TypeScript).

Context: data lives in src/storage/asyncStorage.ts behind the interfaces in src/storage/index.ts. Screens are in src/screens.tsx, plus src/NotesScreen.tsx, src/DocumentsScreen.tsx and src/CardsScreen.tsx. The add/edit sheets are src/PasswordSheet.tsx, src/BirthdaySheet.tsx, src/CardSheet.tsx and src/DocumentSheet.tsx, built on src/DraggableSheet.tsx.

Fix exactly these:

1. WEAK RANDOMNESS. src/PasswordSheet.tsx generates passwords with Math.random(), which is not cryptographically secure. Replace it with a secure source (add react-native-get-random-values and use crypto.getRandomValues). Also use the secure source for the record IDs in src/storage/asyncStorage.ts instead of Date.now() + Math.random().

2. STORAGE ERRORS LOOK LIKE EMPTY DATA. The list() methods catch errors and return [], so a read failure looks like "no data" and a later save can overwrite real records. Make reads fail loudly (let the error propagate) and handle it in the screens with an error state instead of seeding or overwriting.

3. DEMO DATA COMES BACK. src/screens.tsx seeds sample records whenever stored.length === 0, so deleting the last item resurrects the demo data. Seed the demo data only once (persist a "seeded" flag in storage) and never again.

4. PASSWORD AGE IS WRONG. Vault health measures password age from the record's creation time. Track when the password was last changed (a changedAt field, updated whenever the password value changes) and use that instead.

5. SAVE CLOSES BEFORE IT PERSISTS. The sheets call onSave and then close immediately, so if persistence fails the edit is lost silently. Await the save, close only on success, and surface an error otherwise.

6. ORPHANED PHOTOS. When a document is deleted its copied photo file stays on disk. Delete the file when the document is deleted or its photo is replaced.

7. SETTINGS ROWS THAT DO NOTHING. Any Settings row that is not wired to real behaviour must be removed or clearly marked as not available. Do not leave switches that do nothing.

Housekeeping (important): no temporary or patch files (.diff, .patch, .orig, .rej, .bak or editor backups), and no reasoning or thinking-out-loud comments in the code.

Constraints: TypeScript; npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test must pass; you MAY add react-native-get-random-values and no other new dependency.

tasks.title: Documents: expiry dates, expiring soon, and document packs
tasks.prompt:
Continue the Tijori React Native app. Build on the existing Documents section (src/DocumentsScreen.tsx, src/DocumentSheet.tsx, src/storage/) - read it first and extend it rather than recreating it.

Task:
1. Give each document an optional expiry date, using a date picker (reuse src/Calendar.tsx).
2. Add an 'Expiring soon' section at the top of the Documents screen listing documents expiring within the next 90 days, with the number of days remaining. No push notifications.
3. Add document packs: a small set of ready-made checklists (for example Passport application, Bank KYC, Driving licence) showing which required document types the user already has and which are missing. A pack is satisfied when every required type is present.
4. Add unit tests for any new storage logic.

Keep the existing visual language and keep the change additive.

Housekeeping: no temporary or patch files (.diff, .patch, .orig, .rej, .bak or editor backups), and no reasoning or thinking-out-loud comments in the code.

Constraints: TypeScript; npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test must pass; do not add new dependencies.

tasks.title: Notes editor: tap-anywhere cursor, reliable format toggles, and a keyboard-safe layout
tasks.prompt:
Improve the Notes editor in the Tijori React Native app (React Native 0.81.5, TypeScript, Hermes). The editor is src/NoteEditorScreen.tsx plus src/RichEditor.tsx (a WebView with a contenteditable surface), mounted from src/NotesScreen.tsx and shown inside App.tsx, which keeps its NavBar and TabBar visible. Read those files first and change only what is needed.

Fix exactly these three issues, plus one layout tidy-up.

1. CURSOR ON TAP. Today the caret only appears when you tap directly on the text block; tapping the blank writing area does nothing. Make the whole writing area focus the editor on tap, placing the caret at the end of the note's text, or at the start when the note is empty.

2. FORMAT TOGGLES. The B / I / U / S, list and heading buttons must toggle reliably: tapping an active format turns it off, and the button highlight must always reflect the format at the current selection or caret. The current code keeps a saved selection and calls document.execCommand, but that selection is lost when the native toolbar takes focus, so a second tap often fails to un-toggle and stacking formats misbehaves. Rework it so the selection survives use of the toolbar and the button state is re-queried after every change. Several formats must be allowed at once (for example bold and italic together).

3. KEYBOARD MUST NOT HIDE THE TEXT. Keep the app NavBar and TabBar visible, but when the keyboard opens, scroll the caret into view and keep enough bottom padding that the line being typed stays visible above the keyboard.

4. LAYOUT. Move the note title into the app's main NavBar, replacing the word 'Notes' while editing, to free vertical space. Keep the formatting toolbar as a single horizontally-scrolling bar docked at the bottom, riding just above the keyboard.

Constraints: TypeScript; npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test must pass; keep the existing Apple-style visual language and gold accent; do not add new dependencies.

Housekeeping: no temporary or patch files (.diff, .patch, .orig, .rej, .bak or editor backups), and no reasoning or thinking-out-loud comments in the code.
